as_told.title: Narrator clip: the commander in trance sends the group to the window

plain: In 1959, at the National Photographic Interpretation Center, a government office in Washington that analysed photographs, a group of officials is said to have watched someone channel an alien, and then to have seen a flying saucer out the window. The UFO researcher Grant Cameron tells it twice on the show, linking it to Arthur Lundahl, who ran the center. He says the channeler started with automatic writing, meaning writing in a trance supposedly guided by someone else. When Lundahl asked for proof, the channeler switched to speaking aloud and said to go to the window. There, according to Cameron, 'this flying saucer goes flying across in front of the capital.' Cameron dates the meeting to July 9, 1959, cites an 11-page memo on it, and mentions Frances Swan and others connected to the story. A second, unnamed narrator in the same episode tells it more cautiously, saying 'the commander, still in a trance,' sent them to the window, where they 'supposedly observed a UFO', and names no one. If true, it would mean government photo analysts took a channeled contact seriously enough to test it, and believed it passed.
